name: Backhand serve
summary: A compact serve from in front of the body: easy to learn, quick to recover from.
whenToUse: From the middle or backhand side when you want to be close and ready for a fast third ball.

keyPoints.stance: Square to the table, near the middle of the end line.
keyPoints.bodyAction: Small turn back with the toss, then forward.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Short: from the left side of the body across to the front (from the right side if left-handed).
keyPoints.timing: Contact as the ball falls, in front of the body, near table height.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Middle or backhand side, close to the table.
keyPoints.freeArm: Legal toss in front of you, then away.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow forward and up; the wrist snaps at contact. Under the ball for backspin, around the side for sidespin.
keyPoints.recovery: You are already close to ready: just reset the bat.
keyPoints.anticipation: Plan for a fast return to your backhand.

cues: Ball in front of your body

learningPath.task: Watch the elbow lead and the wrist snap.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along: toss in front, compact swing.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Was the toss legal and in front?

learningPath.task: Short backspin and long sidespin backhand serves.

gamePatterns.situation: You are a close-to-table backhand player.
gamePatterns.how: Short backhand serve, then block or punch the third ball with your backhand.

fixes: Let the wrist snap at contact
Let the ball drop, bend the knees
Toss in front and keep it visible

penholdNotes: Penholders usually serve forehand; a backhand serve with the reverse side is possible.
